entityName: MINISDEF - Real Instituto y Observatorio de la Armada (ROA)
entityDescription: The Royal Institute and Observatory of the Spanish Navy, located in San Fernando, Cádiz, is a reference institution in the fields of astronomy and geodesy. Among its capabilities is the Surveillance and Tracking of space objects (SST) using the Fabra-ROA Montsec Telescope (TFRM) and the Laser Ranging Station. The TFRM is a robotic telescope designed for the precise survey of satellites and space debris, allowing for continuous monitoring of these objects. Additionally, the Laser Ranging Station provides extremely accurate distance measurements to satellites, significantly contributing to the improvement of orbital data and the prevention of space collisions. These capabilities position the Royal Observatory of the Navy as a key entity in the safety and sustainability of the space environment.

entityDescription:
Brunel University London, founded in 1966, is a university located in Uxbridge, London, United Kingdom. It was named after the Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel and in2016, Brunel celebrated 50 years as a university.

Brunel is organised into three colleges – Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences; Business, arts and social sciences; and health and life sciences – and three major research institutes – energy futuresand environment; health and societies; and materials and manufacturing.

Brunel is a campus-based university, which means students are never more than 10 minutes away from halls of residence, social and sports facilities, lecture theatres, or the library.

It is also a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities, the European University Association and Universities UK.

Brunel is just a tube ride away from the bustling city of London, making it a go to for students wishing to experience a variety of cultural and social activities.

Its students have access to specialist laboratories for electronic imaging, bioprocessing and experimental techniques, flight, driving and train simulators and a 3D body scanner.

Many undergraduate students may also choose to undertake practical placements and projects as a part of their courses in the form of a sandwich year.

A yearly design exhibition is held by Brunel's Department of Design called ‘Made In Brunel’ to promote and showcase the work of final year students to the rest of the design industry.

Notable alumni include Jo Brand, an English comedian, writer and actress, John McDonnell, a British Labour Party politician who was appointed Shadow Chancellor in September 2015, and Sophie McShera, an English actress.

entityDescription:
Waves Team was founded in 2023 to implement ideas in the field of remote sensing and contact measurements.
Our goal is to develop new and improve existing remote and contact methods for measuring wave parameters and wind speed in the World Ocean and inland waters, measuring the area of the ice cover and assessing its concentration.
Our mission is to develop and promote practical applications of satellite oceanographic information through collaboration with industry, academia and commercial research organizations.
In our activities, we rely on more than 20 years of scientific research experience, including the development of theoretical models and numerical simulations, the development of algorithms for processing satellite data and the retrieving of thematic information, the formation of databases, the development and manufacture of unique underwater acoustic wave gauges for sub-satellite measurements.

We understand that purely satellite solutions rarely provide complete information to users, so we use an integrated approach. This may be a combination of satellite data, numerical models and regional measurements.

entityDescription:
OKRA
Designing meaningful places
We are OKRA: an international and interdisciplinary team in the field of landscape architecture, working from Utrecht, the Netherlands. Together we design and realise resilient landscapes, healthy cities and sustainable water strategies. 
We envision the world of tomorrow as a place with positive impact on people and nature. To attain this, we combine three decades of international experience and thorough research with inventiveness and craftmanship to provide creative, leading and award-winning solutions for today’s and tomorrow’s challenges. 
Our goal is to design resilient landscapes that encourage social life and enhance ecology. We achieve this by adopting an open design approach, drawing inspiration and knowledge beyond given boundaries. Interdisciplinary collaboration and investment in research, both outside and inside the scope of our discipline, are central to our strategy. This allows us to address contemporary issues such as climate resilience, biodiversity, and social inclusiveness.

In our projects, we create valuable, habitable spaces for people and nature. We envisioncities as natural habitats, places where people and nature live together in healthy ways. We conceive innovative solutions and designs forliving with water, empowering sustainable and adaptive ecosystems. Our landscape design process focuses on rediscovering landscapes. In doing so, we uncover and reinterpret physical and historical layers as the basis for new interventions.By uniting nature and culture, we create landscapes that are full of meaning for both. 
OKRA’s multidisciplinary team consists of about 50 landscape architects, urban planners, architects, designers and other specialists. The partners, Martin Knuijt and Wim Voogt, work alongside a team of associates, Tom Wierts, Pierre-Alexandre Marchevet, Rani Izhar, Guiliana Sibilia, Nefeli Kalantzi, Melle van Dijk and Suzanne in ‘t Veld. 
Our specialists work together in dynamic project teams, combining their diverse talents to create high-quality designs. entityDescription: FibreCoat GmbH is a technology-oriented spin-off from the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University, that started its business in February 2020. The researchers involved in FibreCoat were able to use the state-of-the-art machinery at the ITA in order to develop their novel process and patented material. The technological core is a single filament online coating system for glass and basalt fibres during their production with a polymer or aluminum sheath at a production speed of up to 1,000 m/min. The aim of FibreCoat is to supply a novel and innovative lightweight construction preform for composite production. That product will aid in solving the challenges of our modern mobility. The resulting material outperforms any available solutions for thermoplastic composites on the market and can reduce cycle time, costs and weight by up to 50 %. Thus, opening improved lightweight construction for a broad range of applications.

description:
Siranga is set to develop an entirely new kind of image sensing method and devices, photodetectors, and image sensors, collectively called quantum-tunneling imaging photodetectors (QTIP) for a broad range of applications from violet to visible light down to near infrared (NIR) as well as hyperspectral optical detection systems for scientific and industrial applications such as LIDAR. 

The range of applications is extremely wide and spans everything from consumer camera modules through-to imaging systems in satellite Earth observation. The advantage of QTIP is the ultrafast imaging enabling real time monitoring, high sensitivity of the QTIP to low-light applications and the large spectral wavelength range with high sensitivity.

The combination of QTIP with a hyperspectral filter will enable fast real-time monitoring of the food crops, vegetation, deforestation, human migrations, drought, or greenhouse gas emissions. This entirely new technology will contribute to precision farming and digitally automated agriculture, spot detection of global problem areas and other critical applications contributing to alleviating societal and environmental problems.

We envisage next-generation wafer size ~Peta-pixel QTIP sensors for Satellite Earth observation.

Our advances fall into the category of “deep-tech”. Starting from an idea and a vision well founded in the laws of quantum physics. Our resonant quantum tunnelling based cross-grid photodetectors, capable of Tera-pixel imaging is an outstanding example of exploiting the profound and fundamental laws of nature to create instruments for the most practical use cases.

entityDescription:
SpacePharma-EU is located in France in Strasbourg and Sophia-Antipolis. The SpacePharma team is both diverse and experienced, includes experts from both strong Life-Science, Chemistry, Space technology, and international Business Development backgrounds.
OUR VISION: Being a world leader in microgravity research and production solutions by making it accessible, affordable, and reliable serving the biopharma, material sciences, nutrition, agri-tech and chemical industries.
BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: The Life-related Sciences and Industry market (pharmaceutical, cosmetics, biotechnology, materials, food, etc.) needs a low-cost, available, and easily accessible platform to perform complex experiments and manufacturing in microgravity environments. Today there are very limited, often expensive solutions.
SPACEPHARMA’s SOLUTION: innovative miniaturized remotely controlled microfluidics chemistry/biology laboratory on Nanosatellites and space station payload to perform R&D, manufacturing, shorten time-to-market and cut costs for innovative life science applications. SpacePharma provides low cost one-stop-shop end-to-end turnkey upstream, downstream and analytics solution, including:
• In-Orbit Facility (research, development, production).
• Ground station for remotely laboratory control.
• Customer front-end allowing customers to monitor, develop and modify
the experiment procedures and receive experimental data from their 
location on Smartphones.
• Return to Earth if needed.
ACHIEVEMENTS IN SPACE MISSIONS: After a successful experiment demonstrated in parabolic flight in 2016, SpacePharma has launched two Nanosatellites (“DIDO” missions) with full success and advanced lab has already been deployed ten times onboard the ISS– that didn’t require any Astronauts’ operation after setting the lab in place. These deployment methods opened a new era that is meeting the above-mentioned needs while closing the gaps with high User-Friendly End-To-End solution.

SPACEPHARMA’s SOLUTION: innovative miniaturized remotely controlled microfluidics chemistry/biology laboratory on Nanosatellites and space station payload to perform R&D, manufacturing, shorten time-to-market and cut costs for innovative life science applications. SpacePharma provides low cost one-stop-shop end-to-end turnkey upstream, downstream and analytics solution, including:
• In-Orbit Facility (research, development, production).
• Ground station for remotely laboratory control.
• Customer front-end allowing customers to monitor, develop and modify
the experiment procedures and receive experimental data from their 
location on Smartphones.
• Return to Earth if needed.
ACHIEVEMENTS IN SPACE MISSIONS: After a successful experiment demonstrated in parabolic flight in 2016, SpacePharma has launched two Nanosatellites (“DIDO” missions) with full success and advanced lab has already been deployed ten times onboard the ISS– that didn’t require any Astronauts’ operation after setting the lab in place. These deployment methods opened a new era that is meeting the above-mentioned needs while closing the gaps with high User-Friendly End-To-End solution.

Smart Shaped s.r.l. is a company founded in 2015 with the aim of facilitating software development in the enterprise sector. With this mission and thanks to specific skills related to software modeling, it dedicated itself in the early years to the creation of a low-code platform that helps and improves the development of Java Enterprise products and the entire software life cycle, which then became a valuable corporate asset. Specialized in the design, development and maintenance of software solutions, it boasts a wide range of products and solutions created for important Italian companies.Smart Shaped is currently focused on research projects that focus on topics related to Key Enabling Technologies and in particular on projects related to blockchain and artificial intelligence. With these research activities, the company invests in training and research through its team, to offer the best opportunities to its customers and partners.The company invests in research and development activities, at least 30% of the staff is involved in activities of this type every year. Society Green Earth (Udruga Zelena Zemlja) is a non-profit organization based in Osijek, operating within the Republic of Croatia, with activities potentially extending beyond its borders. The Society aims to promote the values of civil society, raise awareness of global changes, protect nature and the environment, encourage free and creative expression, and generally improve the quality of life.
The main goals and areas of activity of the Society include:
- Democratic political culture
- Economy
- Culture and art
- Human rights
- International cooperation
- Education, science, and research
- Sustainable development
- Social activities
- Technical culture
- Nature and environmental protection
The Society achieves its goals through various activities such as nature and environmental protection, citizen education, promotion of social values, encouragement of arts and culture, and providing social assistance and support.
The Society's economic activities include:
- Publishing activities
- Organization of educational, recreational, and tourist activities
- Organization of camps, festivals, and sports events
- Creation of studies and analyses
- Providing consulting services and report preparation
- Production and sale of products
- Organization of courses, seminars, and conferences
The Society's work is public and is ensured through timely reporting to members, use of information and communication technologies, public events, and other appropriate means.
